1	## AR-001: Green-check gate greps for the exact strings this change must delete
2	- Severity: High
3	- References: CHANGE_REQUEST.md AC set; .uncle/workflow/green-check.commands:3-4; BASELINE_REPORT.md section 8-9; CHANGE_PLAN.md "Verification commands"
4	- Failure: green-check cmd3 `grep -c "unclehq/stagegate\|brianosaurus/agentic-workflow" frontend/public/home.html` and cmd4 `grep -c "Claude builds, Codex audits" AGENTIC_WORKFLOW_STRATEGY.md frontend/public/home.html` currently match (exit 0, counts 2 and 1/1 per baseline). `grep -c` exits 1 when zero lines match. A correct AC-1/AC-3 fix removes every occurrence, so both commands will exit nonzero post-fix — the driver's own protected gate fails exactly when the plan succeeds. CHANGE_PLAN.md never reconciles this; it defines separate ad hoc grep commands with inverted expectations instead of addressing the shared gate.
5	- Fix: plan must state that green-check commands 3-4 are baseline-diagnostic (pre-change) probes, not pass/fail assertions the driver enforces post-change, or the driver config must be updated/exempted for this stage. Do not weaken AC-1/AC-3 to keep old strings present.
6	- Verify: run `.uncle/workflow/green-check.commands` cmd3 and cmd4 against the post-edit files and confirm the driver's runner does not treat their nonzero exit as a build failure.
7	
8	## AR-002: AC-7's network-fetch prerequisite has no fallback path
9	- Severity: Medium
10	- References: CHANGE_SPEC.md AC-7, section 16 UNRESOLVED item; CHANGE_PLAN.md step 1
11	- Failure: step 1 requires fetching `github.com/unclehq/uncle` README before any file edit and step 2 depends on step 1. BASELINE_REPORT.md section 9 notes no network access was exercised at baseline and fastapi itself isn't installed in the ambient python3. If the implementation runner also lacks network/WebFetch access, step 1 blocks indefinitely with no stated fallback, contradicting the requirement that build/verification work must not stall on unavailable live-test prerequisites.
12	- Fix: add a fallback: if the README cannot be fetched, state that in the PR/implementation notes as an open assumption and proceed with the CR's own description of uncle (CHANGE_REQUEST.md lines 24-26) rather than blocking.
13	- Verify: confirm the implementing agent has a working fetch tool before treating step 1 as complete; absent that, confirm a documented fallback was used instead of a stalled task.
14	
15	## AR-003: AC-5 tag-line check accepts a cosmetic edit as compliant
16	- Severity: Low
17	- References: CHANGE_SPEC.md AC-5; CHANGE_PLAN.md Traceability row AC-5
18	- Failure: verification is "grep confirms line no longer reads exactly the old B-4 text." A one-character change (e.g., adding a space) satisfies the grep while leaving the tag inaccurate, so incorrect behavior (tag still misdescribes uncle) can pass verification.
19	- Fix: add a positive-content check, e.g. grep for terms drawn from uncle's actual scope (agent-agnostic, terminal, PR) in the tag line, not just absence of the old string.
20	- Verify: assert the new tag line matches at least one uncle-scope keyword, not merely differs from the old text.
21	
22	## AR-004: AC-3 phrase grep can miss a reworded fixed-pairing claim
23	- Severity: Low
24	- References: CHANGE_SPEC.md AC-3, IX-3; CHANGE_PLAN.md Verification commands line 3
25	- Failure: grep targets literal phrases `claude builds|codex audits|claude/codex`. Copy stating e.g. "built with Claude and reviewed by Codex" avoids all three literal phrases yet still describes a fixed pairing, defeating IX-3 while the grep reports pass.
26	- Fix: pair the grep with the manual read already specified in section 18 explicitly covering AC-3 (not just AC-2/AC-6), checking for any fixed-tool-pairing claim, not just the three phrases.
27	- Verify: manual re-read of both files' final prose confirms no fixed-pairing claim in any wording, independent of the grep result.
28	
29	## Overall assessment
30	
31	Plan is executable for AC-1/AC-2/AC-5/AC-8/AC-9 but AR-001 is a blocking contradiction between the required content change and the wired automated gate; it must be resolved (gate reinterpretation or exemption, not weakened acceptance criteria) before implementation is accepted as verifiable. AR-002 threatens step 1 completion if network access is unavailable. AR-003/AR-004 are verification-strength gaps, not blockers.
